name: Artlogic
subcategory: art gallery inventory, CRM and websites
tagline: Inventory, contacts, sales and hosted websites for commercial galleries, artists and collections.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The heart of Artlogic is a well-shaped database: artworks with editions, dimensions, provenance and images, linked to contacts, consignments, offers and invoices. An agent can build that for one artist or one small program in a weekend, and it will feel better than a spreadsheet immediately. Where it falls apart is everything hanging off the edges: the hosted gallery website and artist sites, private viewing rooms clients actually open, feeds out to Artsy, Artnet and Ocula, art fair paperwork, multi-currency VAT invoicing and the mobile app people use while hanging a show. Also worth saying out loud: this is the system of record for objects worth six figures, and a DIY box under someone's desk is a bad place for that. Build it if you are a solo artist tracking your own work; think harder if you are a gallery with staff and consignors.
coreLoopDIY: A local artwork inventory with artists, works, images, contacts, consignments and PDF invoices, plus shareable private viewing room links.
requirements: local disk for high-res image storage and thumbnails
a domain and small VPS if you want viewing room links to work outside your LAN
whatYouLose: Hosted gallery and artist websites that stay in sync with inventory
Distribution feeds to Artsy, Artnet, Ocula and art fair viewing platforms
Polished private viewing rooms and email campaigns collectors will actually open
Art fair, consignment and shipping paperwork built by people who know the trade
Multi-user roles, audit trails, multi-currency VAT invoicing and someone else's backups
moatNotes: The inventory record is easy; being the record that other art-world platforms already read from is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a gallery's inventory database is load-bearing and boring in the best way: it feeds the website, the viewing rooms, the fair submissions, the invoices and the consignment reports, and every one of those has a deadline attached. Artlogic has spent years absorbing the specific weirdness of the trade, editions and AP numbers, works on consignment from three parties, price on request, currency at time of sale, and that accumulated weirdness is what you are actually renting. Add staff logins, someone else running backups, and the fact that migrating fifteen years of records with images is a project nobody wants, and the subscription stops looking expensive.
notes: Perfect for one artist and one studio; a gallery with consignors and a fair calendar should keep paying.
prompt:
Build a local-first art inventory and CRM app called Studio Ledger. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3 with Drizzle ORM, Tailwind for UI, no auth provider, no cloud services, no telemetry.

Data model:
- artists: name, bio, notes
- artworks: title, artist, year, medium, dimensions (h/w/d + unit), edition info (edition number, edition size, AP flag), status (available, on hold, consigned, sold, not for sale), cost, list price, currency, location, provenance notes, private notes
- images: multiple per artwork, uploaded to ./data/uploads, generate 400px and 1600px derivatives with sharp on upload
- contacts: name, email, phone, type (collector, curator, institution, press), notes, tags
- interactions: dated notes linked to a contact and optionally an artwork
- consignments: artwork, counterparty contact, direction (in/out), start date, end date, agreed split
- invoices: contact, line items referencing artworks, currency, discount, notes; render to PDF

UI:
- Inventory grid with thumbnails, plus filters by artist, status, year, price range, and full-text search over title, medium and notes
- Artwork detail page with image gallery, inline edit, status history, linked interactions and consignments
- Contacts list and detail with interaction timeline and works they own or have been offered
- Viewing rooms: pick artworks, set a title and intro text, generate a public /vr/[token] page with a random 32-char token, no login, optional price visibility toggle, and a view counter
- CSV import for artworks and contacts, CSV export for everything
- Invoice PDF generation server-side

Out of scope, do not build: email sending, payments, multi-user accounts, Artsy or Artnet feeds, a public marketing website, a mobile app.

Operational requirements:
- All data in ./data/studio.db, all uploads in ./data/uploads
- A `npm run backup` script that zips ./data with a timestamped filename
- Seed script with 3 artists, 12 artworks and 5 contacts so the UI is not empty
- Any secrets (only PUBLIC_BASE_URL and an optional VIEWING_ROOM_SALT) go in .env, with .env.example committed
- README covering setup, backup, restore, and a blunt warning that this is a single-user local tool with no access control beyond viewing room tokens
